title: The Word She Could Write — Pure Alexia From Déjerine & Landolt (1892) to Pre-/Postsurgical VWFA Word-Length Slopes, Visual Span Limits & Reversible Cortical Stimulation (2025)

teenKit.tldr: Pure alexia is a bizarre neurological glitch where people can write words perfectly fine but completely lose the ability to read them back. It proves that reading and writing live in totally separate physical neighborhoods inside your brain.
teenKit.whyItMatters: Understanding how a tiny brain bottleneck breaks our ability to process words reveals how consciousness builds complex skills out of separate, specialized wiring.
keyTakeaways: Reading and writing are not a single bundled package; your brain can keep its writing ability completely intact while losing the machinery to decode visual letters.
The Visual Word Form Area (VWFA) acts as a specialized processing hub in the left side of the brain that translates raw visual squiggles into recognizable words.
Cutting-edge 2025 neuroscience has proven this by using direct electrical stimulation to temporarily switch a patient's reading ability on and off in real time without touching their writing.

vocab.meaning: A condition also known as alexia without agraphia, where a person can write normally but cannot read what they wrote.
A specific region in the left occipitotemporal part of the brain that acts as the ultimate visual recognition hub for reading words.
The frustrating delay added to reading time for every extra letter in a word, showing up heavily when the brain's fast word-recognition network is damaged.
Applying a tiny electrical current directly to specific brain tissue to momentarily disrupt or test its function during surgery.

quiz.question: If a person has pure alexia, what happens when you ask them to write a word and then read it?
options: They can write the word easily, but they cannot read it back and see it only as meaningless ink squiggles.
They can read any word on a page, but their hands completely forget how to hold a pen.
They lose all language abilities, including speaking and listening comprehension.
They can read and write normally, but only if the words are written in cursive.
quiz.explanation: Pure alexia specifically decouples input from output, allowing people to write words flawlessly while failing entirely to decode them visually.

quiz.question: What is the primary function of the Visual Word Form Area (VWFA) in the human brain?
options: Controlling the fine motor skills required to form letters with a pen.
Translating spoken sounds into inner thoughts.
Acting as a specialized node that instantly recognizes and processes written words.
Regulating the speed at which our eyes move across a digital screen.
quiz.explanation: The VWFA serves as a critical neural hub dedicated to instantly decoding visual letter strings into meaningful language.

quiz.question: How did modern researchers in 2025 take this neurological discovery to the next level?
options: By analyzing ancient medical journals from 19th-century Paris.
By using reversible intracerebral electrical stimulation to temporarily induce pure alexia in real time.
By training artificial intelligence to write cursive without human hands.
By proving that reading and writing are actually controlled by the exact same group of neurons.
quiz.explanation: Recent surgical studies successfully used direct electrical brain stimulation to momentarily switch reading off while leaving writing completely spared.
